company_info.industry_info: Software Development / Enterprise Open Source. Canonical is the publisher of Ubuntu, one of the most widely used Linux distributions, and provides open source security, support and services covering critical systems from IoT devices to cloud infrastructure, including databases, containers, AI, and Kubernetes solutions.
company_info.recent_news: In June 2025, Canonical published a financial report showing revenue for 2024 amounted to $291 million (up from $251 million in 2023). The company's gross profit for 2024 was $258.3 million with operating profit of $15.5 million, demonstrating strong profitability and growth. No recent layoffs found.
company_info.company_culture: Canonical is a remote-first company since inception in 2004 with no traditional offices. Employee reviews highlight: true 100% remote work environment, good work-life balance, flexible working hours, capable and smart teammates, free travel to twice-yearly in-person team sprints globally. Positive signals include focus on open source, international culture, and distributed collaboration. Some concerns noted in reviews: compensation is lower compared to top tech companies, and career growth can sometimes stall due to timezone challenges.
company_info.any_related_information: Canonical is founder-led by Mark Shuttleworth (CEO) and is profitable and growing. The company pioneered global distributed collaboration and expects high standards of excellence. Known for hiring on a global basis with rigorous selection standards. Long interview process noted in employee reviews. Mark Shuttleworth previously attempted an IPO in 2023. Ubuntu is used extensively in enterprise initiatives including public cloud, data science, AI, and IoT, with customers including world's leading public cloud and silicon providers.
